title: Equality-constrained lower level: primitive gradients and the outer gradient mapping
summary: Let $h(x,y)=Ax-By-b$, $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y:\,h(x,y)=0}g(x,y)$, and $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$. Seek the following approximate stationarity criterion for $\min_{x\in X}\Phi(x)$.

task.detail: min_{x in X} Phi(x) with h(x,y*)=0.
description_paragraphs: Let $h(x,y)=Ax-By-b$, $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y:\,h(x,y)=0}g(x,y)$, and $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$. Seek the following approximate stationarity criterion for $\min_{x\in X}\Phi(x)$.

model.objects: Phi(x)=f(x,y*(x)); y* uniquely minimizes g(x,y) over the declared lower feasible set.
model.regularity: f is jointly C_f-smooth and L_f-Lipschitz; g is jointly C_g-smooth and mu_y-strongly convex in y.
model.constraints: Public A in R^{d_h x d_x}, B in R^{d_h x d_y}, b in R^{d_h}; h(x,y)=Ax-By-b. B has full row rank, with public lower singular-value bound beta_B>0 and public ||A||,||B|| bounds.
model.initialization: Public x0,y0; Phi(x0)-inf Phi<=Delta, and a public lower-solution initial-distance bound R_y for cost constants/logarithms.
model.geometry: Euclidean norms; constraint matrices/data are known, not hidden oracle outputs.
model.outer_feasible: Public nonempty compact convex X with exact projection Pi_X available and diameter bound D_X.
model.regularity_extra: The full Hessian of g is S_g-Lipschitz on X x R^{d_y}. Public C_H bounds the inverse KKT matrix on the relevant solution graph; it is controlled by strong convexity and constraint conditioning.
description_paragraphs: The function $f$ has $C_f$-Lipschitz joint gradient and is $L_f$-Lipschitz in value. The function $g$ has $C_g$-Lipschitz joint gradient and is $\mu_y$-strongly convex in $y$. All norms are Euclidean or their induced operator norms.

Inputs $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d_h\times d_x}$, $B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_h\times d_y}$, and $b\in\mathbb{R}^{d_h}$ are public. The matrix $B$ has full row rank and smallest singular value at least the public $\beta_B>0$. The initial point has upper-level gap at most $\Delta$ and lower-level initial distance at most $R_y$.

The set $X$ is nonempty, compact, and convex with diameter at most $D_X$. The full Hessian of $g$ is $S_g$-Lipschitz on $X\times\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Along the solution graph, the inverse lower-level KKT matrix has the public uniform bound $C_H$.
model.outer_geometry: The reduced objective may be nonconvex. Its differentiability or local Lipschitz regularity is specified by the model and accuracy measure.

operations: Choose f or g at (x,y); receive exact full gradient.
oracle.query_domain: x in X and y in R^{d_y}; the regularity promises and all legal queries use this fixed domain.
oracle.auxiliary: Known affine constraint operations, exact affine projections, and Pi_X are available; no free y*(x), multiplier or Hessian.
description_paragraphs: Choose $f$ or $g$ and obtain its exact full gradient at an admissible pair $(x,y)$, where $x\in X$ and $y\in\mathbb R^{d_y}$.

Operations with the known linear constraints and their projections are free. The interface $\Pi_X$ is also available, with its count recorded separately. Lower-level solutions, active sets, and hypergradients are not supplied by default.
Return an outer point $\widehat{x}\in X$, possibly unqueried. Neither an inner point nor a certificate is required.

Define $\mathcal{G}_\tau(x)=\tau^{-1}[x-\Pi_X(x-\tau\nabla\Phi(x))]$ and error $\|\mathcal{G}_\tau(\widehat{x})\|$. The step size $0<\tau\le1/L_\Phi$ is public and fixed; $L_\Phi$ bounds reduced-gradient Lipschitz continuity.

resource.projection: First-order cost Q=N_grad_f+N_grad_g; projections are separately recorded and have zero cost only in this declared query model.
description_paragraphs: Retain the primitive call counts at both levels and the outer projection count. The scalar gradient cost is $N=N_{\nabla f}+N_{\nabla g}$, with projections recorded separately. Every call in an approximate inner solve counts toward the fixed budget.

Algorithms are deterministic and may use arbitrary measurable adaptive queries, stopping, and postprocessing. Outputs may be unqueried, deterministically selected historical points, or admissible averages. No span or zero-respecting restriction applies. Queries are sequential; each response in a batch is charged. Internal arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage are free, with no separate work, memory, or communication budget.
The condition $\|\mathcal{G}_\tau(\widehat{x})\|\le\varepsilon$ holds deterministically on each instance.

notes: Combine $\|D_xy^*\|\le C_J$ and $\operatorname{Lip}(D_xy^*)\le C_HS_g(1+C_J)^2$ to obtain $L_\Phi$. This retains the $C_f$ term when $S_g=0$, avoiding degeneration of the source displayed formula at that endpoint.

Compute each hypergradient proxy to uniform error $O(\varepsilon)$ and select the smallest computable approximate gradient mapping. This provides a deterministic output for each instance. Accelerated gradient descent solves the strongly convex inner problems to the required accuracy.
